title.narrative: Training on green house gas (GHG) mitigation

description.narrative: The project aims to provide Ukrainian businesses and environmental communities with knowledge necessary to reduce GHG (Green House Gas) emissions as well as raise their awareness of the climate change problems and empower their actions for GHG emissions mitigation. Specifically, after the project implementation, Ukrainian businesses will have a much better understanding on how to export goods to the EU covered by the Carbon Border Adjusted Mechanisms (CBAM)-register and will be able to start this activity; and will be ready to join future Ukrainian Emission Trading Systems. The project has a positive impact on:SDG 8: inclusive and sustainable economic growth: support productive activities, decent job creation, entrepreneurship, creativity and innovation.SDG 13: Climate action: national climate policies, and resources to create awareness and support for climate change mitigation measures to reduce GHG emissions.

comment.narrative:
The project considers three results: (1) the design of training on GHG emissions for digital implementation targeting private businesses; (2) Communication outreach and selection of participants, ensuring a wide representation of Ukrainian SMEs and economic sectors; and including youth and women entrepreneurs; (3) implementation of the training on GHG emissions mitigation. • The training focused primarily on medium-sized businesses operating in intermediary cities, towns and rural areas that need to join the carbon pricing/carbon accounting system, which is new for Ukraine, and partly also for the EU CBAM (cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen). • The content of the training included five thematic blocks that were implemented in 5 weeks: Climate policy of Ukraine and the European Union; EU Emission trading system (ETS) and UA ETS; Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM); CBAM in Ukraine’s context; Measures for GHG emissions reduction in sectors under CBAM and MRV system. Overall, the project, enabled that businesses and environmental communities increased their awareness of European climate policy and their impact on access to European markets. In addition, through the online training the businesses developed capabilities to reduce GHG emissions, which is a particularly urgent task for Ukraine to ensure access to external markets.
